arms.name: Question-mode (Q)
arms.description: Human-led question mode: the participant supplies an initial unassisted idea; GPT-4.1 supplies knowledge or an analogy and asks questions to elicit alternatives, then asks elaboration questions before the participant submits the refined idea. This follows the Table 5 prompts and Figure 2; Section 4.2 instead describes the model as generating the alternatives.

arms.name: Suggestion-mode (S)
arms.description: Human-led suggestion mode: GPT-4.1 supplies alternative ideas and elaboration suggestions after an unassisted initial idea; the participant refines and submits the final idea.

arms.name: Model-led (M)
arms.description: Model-led one-shot refinement: GPT-4.1 rewrites the participant initial idea to increase originality, usefulness and elaboration; the participant may further refine the model output before submission.

arms.name: Vanilla (V)
arms.description: Free chat with GPT-4.1 in the same chat interface, without additional system prompts or intervention logic; participants could formulate or copy and paste the final idea.

arms.name: Control (C)
arms.description: Participants generate and refine their idea without LLM support.

studies.task: Generate and refine one creative idea repurposing existing car features for new uses beyond their original purpose in vehicles.

ai_tool.name: GPT-4.1 via the OpenAI API (snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14)
ai_tool.locator: PDF p. 6, Section 4.2: all LLM-assisted conditions used GPT-4.1, snapshot gpt-4.1-2025-04-14; PDF p. 19, Table 5 note. The Vanilla row in Table 5 inconsistently says Standard GPT-4.

preregistration.primary_outcome: Idea quality, diversity of the idea pool, and perceived idea ownership are the primary outcomes named in PDF p. 7, Section 4.4, with preregistered hypotheses in Sections 3 and 4.5. The paper does not rank one above the others.

estimates.outcome: Idea quality (expert mean of originality and usefulness)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Consensual Assessment Technique: four domain experts independently rated originality and usefulness on seven-point scales; ratings across dimensions and raters were averaged to one score per idea. Each participant supplied one scored idea (only the first idea was judged if more than one was supplied). PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 22, Appendix D.

estimates.outcome: Idea diversity (cosine distance to leave-one-out condition centroid)
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; per-idea cosine distance to the leave-one-out centroid of the other final ideas within the same experimental condition. Higher distance means greater across-person diversity. One scored final idea per participant. PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 8, footnote 2.

estimates.notes: Arm means, SDs and analyzed people counts are transcribed from Table 2. SDs are across the scored outputs, one output per participant, so output-level and participant-level variation coincide here. The contrast-specific total people/output count is not printed and is left null; no arm counts were summed. Section 4.4 defines cosine distance and the results interpret higher values as more diverse, despite similarity terminology in the Table 2 note and Appendix H. estimates.notes: Arm means, SDs and analyzed people counts are transcribed from Table 2. SDs are across the scored outputs, one output per participant, so output-level and participant-level variation coincide here. The contrast-specific total people/output count is not printed and is left null; no arm counts were summed. Alternative specification of the same outcome and participants as the corresponding main Table 3 record; not an independent sample. Dunn’s post hoc rank test following Kruskal–Wallis. stats.p_value is the printed Holm-adjusted one-sided p_adj; the unadjusted one-sided p is .013, from the p column in the same verbatim source row. The appendix describes adjustment across all pairwise comparisons. The r effect size is transcribed; its formula/standardizer is not stated. preregistered_primary refers to the outcome, not to this robustness specification.

Higher distance means greater across-person diversity. One scored final idea per participant. PDF p. 7, Section 4.4; PDF p. 8, footnote 2. Appendix H applies a logit transformation before the parametric robustness test.

estimates.notes: Contrast-specific totals are not printed; counts have not been summed. Section 4.4 defines cosine distance and the results interpret higher values as more diverse, despite similarity terminology in the Table 2 note and Appendix H. The paper treats each person once in the main analysis, but the distances share condition centroids; it does not report uncertainty that recomputes those centroids under participant resampling. Alternative specification of the same sample and primary diversity outcome. No arm mean, SD, SE, raw difference, or confidence interval on the logit scale is printed, so those fields are null. Original cosine-distance means and SDs are retained in s1_diversity_s_vs_v; they are not mixed with the transformed test here. The table provides t, degrees of freedom, p and Cohen’s d; the d standardizer is not stated. preregistered_primary refers to the outcome, not to this robustness specification.

estimates.outcome: Between-arm difference in initial-to-refined idea-diversity change
estimates.question: across_people
estimates.measure_detail: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large cosine distance: initial and refined ideas are evaluated against the centroid of initial ideas in their own condition, with leave-one-out initial distances. The outcome is the change from the unassisted initial idea to the refined idea produced with AI available. Both arm means below are estimated mean changes, not final-idea levels. PDF pp. 8-9, Section 5.3 and footnote 2; PDF p. 10, Figure 6; PDF p. 24, Tables 12-13.

stats.difference_is: As printed: control minus treatment in refined-minus-initial change (opposite to the named treatment-minus-control ordering).

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model of idea diversity with interaction mode, time and mode-by-time interactions; Question-Mode and initial idea are reference levels, with a participant random intercept. The recorded term is Model-Led × Time. It estimates the named control-arm change minus the Question-mode treatment-arm change.

sources.locator: PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 13, Question-mode row (Change and SE)
PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 13, Model-led (M) row (Change and SE)
PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 12, Model-Led × Time fixed-effect row
PDF p. 24, Appendix G, Table 12, interval-column heading

estimates.notes: Exploratory comparison of change between individually randomized AI arms; this is not a randomized-order crossover. within_person is null because the qualifying comparison is between randomized arms. The initial-to-refined order is fixed. The paper does not print the sample size for this mixed model; no counts are inferred from degrees of freedom or borrowed from Table 2. Question-mode is the tested human-led configuration and is named treatment as in the screening form. IMPORTANT SIGN: Table 12 uses Question-Mode as the regression reference and prints the other arm minus Question-Mode. The coefficient, t-statistic and CI retain this printed sign, which is the reverse of treatment minus control. difference_is explicitly records that orientation; no sign has been calculated or changed. Arm levels and arm SEs come from Table 13 and are estimated refined-minus-initial changes. The interaction coefficient and its uncertainty come from Table 12; arm changes have not been subtracted. The mean-change levels in Table 13 are not interchangeable with final-idea centroid distances in Table 2. The model includes participant random intercepts, but the condition-centroid dependence is not explicitly addressed.

open_items: Study 2 random assignment remains unconfirmed: the saved PDF describes a replication but no allocation mechanism (PDF pp. 10-11, Section 6.1). Its outcomes are excluded pending confirmation; do not infer randomization from the Study 1 procedure or the label experiment.

The paper gives the main randomized experiment count in Section 4 and the final analyzed count in Section 4.3; the abstract and Figure 1 use the final count when describing assignment. Per-arm randomized counts and per-arm exclusions are not printed.

The main Cohen’s d standardizer is not specified in the PDF, and the contrast SEs and confidence intervals promised in Section 4.5 are not printed in Table 3. Participant-equivalent arm SDs are available in Table 2.
Table 3 and Section 5.1.2 disagree on the H2b p-value and H3a Cohen’s d. Table values are used and the alternative prose is preserved in the relevant records.

Tables 12-13 do not print the mixed-model analysis sample or degrees of freedom for its interaction coefficients. The degrees of freedom printed for within-arm changes in Section 5.3 do not establish the sample for the interaction model; all its counts and interaction degrees of freedom are left null.

Tables 12 and 13 differ slightly for the Question-mode time contrast, and Section 5.3 differs from Table 13 for the Suggestion-mode t-statistic. Table 13 supplies arm mean changes/SEs and Table 12 supplies the between-arm interactions; the discrepancies have not been recalculated or reconciled.

The Table 12 mode-by-time coefficients are printed in the reverse direction of the named treatment/control arms. Downstream code must use difference_is and the regression-model description before assigning effect direction.

Diversity scores share condition centroids. The paper uses one idea per participant in the main model and participant random intercepts for change, but does not quantify uncertainty from estimating the centroids. No AI-versus-control diversity inferential test is printed.

Question-mode implementation descriptions differ between Section 4.2 and the prompts/Figure 2; the Vanilla row of Table 5 also differs from the stated common GPT-4.1 model. The arm descriptions prioritize the actual prompts and the common-model statement while retaining these conflicts.

The coded elaboration-depth subset is excluded under the full-sample extraction rule; its arm means are figure-only. No means or category proportions have been calculated from the printed qualitative percentages.
notes: Extraction by B from the saved PDF, with all markdown characters read in contiguous chunks through the appendices. Every cited numerical page was checked with pymupdf; source quotes are copied directly from its text layer and preserve printed signs and precision. The statistic inventory for eligible output outcomes is Table 2 arm descriptives, Table 3 primary planned contrasts, Table 12 randomized-arm change interactions, Table 13 arm change levels, and Tables 14-15 robustness tests; pooled/omnibus/baseline parameters, fixed-order within-arm changes and subset coding are accounted for in not_extracted. Main and robustness records reuse the same participants and outcomes and must not be treated as independent studies. Table 3 is the main specification; Table 14 and Table 15 analyses are alternative specifications. The preregistered_primary flag refers to whether the outcome is one of the paper’s preregistered primary outcomes, not whether every alternative analysis or descriptive comparison was preregistered. The study AI role is other because roles vary by arm: free chat, model refinement, supplied ideas/suggestions, and questions with knowledge/analogies. The vanilla-versus-control quality record is the general-chat comparison under the codebook; the same diversity comparison is descriptive only. No first-round crossover or after-AI outcome is reported. No differences, standardized effects, standard errors, totals, figure values, or unprinted arm levels were computed. Shared-sample information is absent in the reconciled form.
